chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Tamimi al-Ansari was in Medina, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca. When death approached him, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Muslims were praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). So Al-Bara' bequeathed that when he was buried, his face should be turned towards the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), towards the Qiblah. Thus, the Sunnah was established with it. And he bequeathed a third of his wealth, and the Book (Quran) was revealed concerning it, and the Sunnah was established with it.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: The Sunnah, the established practice or tradition of the Prophet and Imams.
key_terms.الْبَرَاءُ بْنُ مَعْرُورٍ: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, a companion of the Prophet known for his role in the early migration to Medina.
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qiblah, the direction of prayer, which was changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in Mecca.
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: The Book (Quran), referring to the revelation of verses concerning inheritance and the one-third bequest.
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ: Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), the first Qiblah of the Muslims before the change to Mecca.
key_terms.ثُلُثِ مَالِهِ: One-third of his wealth, a specific portion of an estate that can be bequeathed to non-heirs.

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Islamic practice of burying the deceased facing the Qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur’s foresight in aligning his burial orientation with the future Qiblah of Mecca, a practice that became a normative Sunnah in Shia and Sunni jurisprudence. It also connects his specific bequest of one-third of his wealth to the revelation of the inheritance verse (Ayat al-Mirath), illustrating the interplay between prophetic instruction and divine legislation. The narrative underscores the continuity of ritual practice even during the transitional period of the Prophet's migration.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Bara’a Bin Marour Al-Tamimy Al-Ansary was in Al-Medina, and Rasool-Allahsaww was in Makkah, and the death presented itself to him, and Rasool-Allahsaww and the Muslims were praying Salaat (facing) towards Bayt Al-Maqdis. So Bara’a bequeathed that when he is buried, his face be made towards Rasool-Allahsaww , towards the Qiblah. So the Sunnah flowed with it, and he bequeathed with a third of his wealth, and the Book Revealed with it and the Sunnah flowed with it’.
en.sarwar: 16. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur al-Tamimiy al-Ansariy was in al-Madinah and the Messenger of Allah was in Makkah. He died when the Messenger of Allah and Muslims would face Jerusalem during prayer. He said in his will that when he died, the Messenger of Allah should place him facing Qiblah in the grave. This became a Sunnah (tradition). He also said in his will that one-third of his properties should be given to the needy. A verse in the Holy Quran was revealed about one-third of the properties of a deceased and it became an established Sunnah (tradition).”
